title: Which width tells you the insert fits?
hook: Which measurement checks whether this insert fits?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: that the inside width is the outside width minus both walls, so an insert narrower than the box can still be too wide for its inside

misconception: If the box is wider than the insert, the insert fits.
objective: A container’s outer width includes both walls. The insert must fit the clear inside opening, so subtracting the walls can change an apparent fit into a collision.

recall.question: A box is 50 cm wide outside, with 1.5 cm walls. Will a rigid 48 cm insert fit?
options: No, it is 1 cm too wide
recall.why: The insert must fit the clear inside width: 50 − 2 × 1.5 = 47 cm. A 48 cm insert is 1 cm too wide, though the outside measurement looked roomy. Corners and tapers may narrow it further.
